raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a line plot illustrating the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number across five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROMEO. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 0 to 65, with major gridlines at intervals of 5. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 40% accuracy and increases slightly to around 45% as the co-occurrence number increases. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at about 44% and rises to approximately 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method (blue line with downward-pointing triangular markers) starts at roughly 41% and increases to about 48%. The MEMIT method (purple line with square markers) begins at approximately 44% and increases to around 55%. The ROMEO method (green line with square markers) starts at about 52% and shows a steady increase to approximately 65% at the highest co-occurrence number. All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
